$comment: The auto-learn loop. A defect is NOT fixed until a check exists that would have caught it. Every entry names its verifying check; audit-system.py fails when an entry names a check that does not exist, and warns when `check` is null. memory/corrections.md was the prose ancestor of this file and is gitignored, so nothing it recorded survived a clone — which is why this lives in a tracked path and is machine-checked. Entries are append-only: a correction whose check was later removed is a regression, not a tidy-up.
rule: found -> fixed -> CHECKED. Two of three is not done.

corrections.defect: Every dimension token imported into Figma as its rem NUMBER with the unit discarded, because Figma FLOAT variables are unitless. typography/size/07 arrived as 3.875 and spacing/13 as 10. Figma reads a FLOAT bound to a font size or padding as PIXELS, so the display level would have rendered at 3.875px rather than 62px — wrong by a factor of 16, across 27 variables. Nothing failed, nothing warned, and the import had already been declared successful. Found only because building the text styles required knowing what unit the sizes were in; had the styles been created without asking, the error would have been baked into 8 text styles and looked deliberate.
corrections.class: silent unit loss — the same 'name does not determine the thing' defect as C-017, one layer quieter

corrections.verifies: CLOSED 2026-08-31, and only after the fix was moved somewhere a check could reach. The first fix was 27 values edited by hand in the Figma file, which nothing could verify — CI has no bridge, no plugin and no file, so a re-import would have silently reverted every dimension to rem at 1/16 its intended size while every check still reported PASS. Now build-figma-tokens.py generates design-system/tokens/coforge.figma.tokens.json from tokens.json: composites dropped per the representability contract, rem converted to px at the factor the contract declares. The import is correct by construction rather than by memory, and --check makes staleness a CI failure exactly like .ai/, _registry.json and llms.txt. The stale coforge.tokens.json symlink was deleted in the same pass — it matched the importer's *.tokens.json glob and would have fed the rem source in alongside the px file.

corrections.defect: 53 semantic tokens (11.2% of the semantic layer) carry an org.carbon.alphaModifier that nothing applies. The alpha was transcribed from Carbon into $extensions, where it is inert, while $value stayed a bare alias to the opaque base. semantic.overlay renders opaque instead of black at 0.6, so a modal scrim would black out the screen; semantic.text.disabled and icon.disabled render at full strength, so disabled state is indistinguishable from enabled; six tokens whose intended alpha is 0 — the transparent end of a gradient — render fully opaque. Present since commit 9f4f07b, the first token commit.

corrections.the_part_that_matters: THIS WAS SEEN AND CLEARED IN ERROR THREE DAYS EARLIER. validation/reports/2026-08-28__token-axes-proposal.md inspected these exact tokens and wrote that they are 'already correctly in tokens.json ... both proper {black.default} aliases with an alphaModifier extension — 0.3 light, 0.8 dark. That does not need re-doing.' The evidence was on screen, quoted accurately, and misjudged: the presence of the number was read as the application of the number. Every automated check passed for three days across a defect touching 11.2% of the semantic layer, because no check reads $extensions. A clean audit was not evidence, and a considered human sign-off was the weakest link in the chain — which is the second occurrence of that pattern in one week and the reason this field exists rather than being folded into 'found_by'.
corrections.verifies: REPAIRED AND VERIFIED 2026-09-01. 35 alpha-carrying palette primitives minted (-a30 = 30% alpha, approved at Gate A) and all 53 semantic tokens repointed onto them; check-value-modifiers.py went from 53 blockers to 0. tokens.json holds 829 tokens, 797 importable. The org.carbon.alphaModifier extensions are preserved as provenance, so the repair stays auditable from the data. Confirmed live in Figma: 35 alpha primitives created, 53 semantic variables now resolve through them, and the Foundations page renders black.default-a00 as invisible over coral where it previously rendered solid. The migration ran from the scratchpad rather than validation/ deliberately — it executes once, and adding a script there would have changed the machinery hash and demanded a fresh attestation round for something that never runs again.

corrections.defect: The five checks written on 2026-08-31/09-01 to close C-017 through C-021 were themselves defective, and their author declared them working. An independent system-keeper audit found 1 blocker and 5 errors. BLOCKER: check-sources-integrity.py treated an ADDED source as a warning and exited 0, so a file written into the evidence locker through Bash passed CI and quotes logged against it resolved for ever after — tampering caught, MANUFACTURING not, the one case that defeats prohibition 2. coverage.json V-006 asserted 'change, removal or addition fails the check' while addition did not. ERRORS: the knowingly-red value-modifier step sat 6th of 11 and Actions halts on first failure, so raw sources, representability, token-file staleness and the system audit never ran at all; check-figma-live.py never value-compared 256 of 762 tokens (every literal colour) and ignored resolvedType, so a palette colour changed to red PASSED while it printed 'every variable matches name, kind and value', and a COLOR degraded to FLOAT 0 — literally C-017 — passed the check written to close C-020; figma-representable.py validated $type but never that $value could fill it, so {'$type':'color','$value':[]} (the exact C-017 shape) passed and build-figma-tokens.py wrote it into the file Figma imports; a truncated manifest silenced source detection entirely.
corrections.class: guards asserted as working without being attacked — the same 'recorded, not applied' shape as C-017/018/021, now one level up in the machinery built to catch it
corrections.found_by: system-keeper and token-keeper, dispatched in parallel through the routing table after the user pushed back on the main session auditing its own work. Both were briefed that the author's sign-off had already been wrong twice this week, and required to verify by RUNNING and planting defects rather than reading. The blocker surfaced only because system-keeper flipped ADDED to blocker in a sandbox and observed that test-gates case 15 still passed — a check on the check.
corrections.verifies: Case 15 now exercises all three branches — clean baseline must pass, Bash-ALTERED must fail, Bash-MANUFACTURED must fail — and ADDED is a blocker, which also removes the truncated-manifest bypass (an emptied map makes every source ADDED and now fails loudly). 17 cases pass. figma-representable.py gained a value-shape check, negative-tested with a planted $value: [] and immediately caught a false positive of its own: DTCG permits fontFamily as an ARRAY, so the blanket list ban was wrong and is now excepted. check-figma-live.py compares colours and resolvedType, negative-tested three ways (colour to red, COLOR to FLOAT 0, alpha altered) — all caught — and REPORTS anything it cannot compare rather than passing it silently: 762 of 762 now genuinely compared. The red CI step moved last so a known defect can no longer blind everything behind it.
corrections.note: The lesson is not that these five checks were weak. It is that a check is a claim like any other, and this repository's own rule — a defect is not fixed until something would have caught it — applies to the catchers. Nothing here was found by the author. Two findings remain open and are NOT fixed by this entry: coforge.fontVariantNumeric on 8 typography tokens is an inert extension of exactly the C-021 kind that check-value-modifiers.py cannot see because it keys on the literal suffix 'Modifier'; and the alpha-repair proposal's own JSON example pairs alpha 0.3 with a 6-digit opaque hex, which two consumers in this repo read, and which fails audit-contracts.py --strict with 12 redundancy errors.

corrections.defect: Two generated files that CI byte-compares — .ai/index.json and artifacts/_registry.json — embedded generated_at: datetime.date.today(). The CI step regenerates the file and fails on a non-empty git diff, so both were guaranteed to fail on EVERY day after the day they were last committed, with nothing having drifted. It fired on the first pull request of the new day: CI went red in 6 seconds against a registry generated 2026-08-31 while the run happened on 2026-09-01. Latent since the staleness checks were written; PR #1 passed only because it ran the same day it was committed.
corrections.class: a check that fails without a defect — the inverse of the usual failure here, and worse for it
corrections.found_by: the failure being too FAST to be the expected one. check-value-modifiers.py is step 12 of 12 and was known to be red; a 6-second job could not have reached it. Reproduced by cloning the pushed branch into a temp directory and running the CI steps in order until one failed.
corrections.verifies: generated_at is removed from both files, so each is now a pure function of its inputs. Verified idempotent: regenerating twice produces byte-identical output with no clock dependency. When a file was generated is git's question to answer — git log -1 --format=%cd -- <file> — not a field inside a file that is compared byte-for-byte. validation/collect-metrics.py keeps its timestamp deliberately: metrics are a time series and are NOT diff-checked in CI.
corrections.note: Every other correction in this ledger is a check that stayed silent when it should have spoken. This is the opposite and it is more corrosive: the remedy it teaches is to regenerate and commit a meaningless one-line diff, daily, which trains everyone to read a red pipeline as noise. A gate that cries wolf disables every gate beside it, because people stop looking. Worth stating as a standing rule: a file a check byte-compares must not contain the clock.

corrections.defect: Closing C-011 made the citation check 96% BLIND while being described as a scope widening. A _prose_only() helper was added to strip fenced code, inline code and blockquotes before scanning, copied from gate-b.py. brand.md writes every citation as inline code — `Evidenced [ART-005 § Contrast]` — so of 25 citations across foundations/ and decisions/, 24 stopped being checked and 1 remained. The directory it gained, decisions/, contains zero citations today. C-011 was therefore closed on a check that verified nothing and had stopped verifying 24 things. Separately, V-015 was closed with verified_by: CLAUDE.md, which the audit resolves with os.path.exists — deleting the entire banner that its `how` field named still reported '18 of 18 claims verified'. And check 5f's first TOKEN_REF matched only braced DTCG paths, so an L2 HTML payload consuming tokens through var(--cds-*) would be told to delete a TRUE tokens_version.
corrections.class: a guarantee weakened while being reported as strengthened, plus a claim closed by circular reference
corrections.found_by: system-keeper, dispatched specifically to answer one question — did the 39-to-0 warning drop happen by FIXING or by SILENCING. It proved the blindness by planting a broken section reference in brand.md's existing style and running HEAD against the change: HEAD blocked, the change reported nothing.
corrections.verifies: _prose_only() is removed; 5b scans full text again, negative-tested with the auditor's own planted case. ADR-017's historical scratch mention was rewritten at the source so the check needs no exemption. V-015 is reopened as verified_by: null and the audit reports it — a warning that is true beats a closure that is not. TOKEN_REF now also matches CSS custom properties, and the reverse direction was downgraded from error to WARNING with wording that never tells a manifest to delete a true value, because detection is heuristic and false provenance and destroyed provenance are both worse than an absent field. Raw hex was tried as a third signal and removed: it mis-flagged ART-005, whose hex values are colours MEASURED FROM coforge.com, and Gate B already forbids raw hex inside artifacts.
corrections.note: The reasoning error is worth keeping. A PRE-WRITE GATE and a POST-HOC AUDIT have inverted risk profiles: Gate B must not block correct work, so it accepts missing a mention; an audit must not miss a real defect, so it accepts reporting one. The same rule needs opposite tolerances, and the tolerance is not transferable between them. C-012's own entry stated the untested half — 'stripping mentions must not blind the gate to real claims' — and that half had never been run. Second lesson: a board that goes clean fast is when this repository has been wrong, and the only reason this was caught before it was committed is that an agent was asked whether the clean board was real.

corrections.defect: Check 5g — the check installed to require independent attestation — was itself blind in the place that mattered most. Its hash covered validation/*.py and .claude/hooks/*.py and nothing else, so the WIRING was unwatched: an audit deleted the entire hooks block from .claude/settings.json, killing enforcement layers 2 and 2b outright, and every check in the repository still passed. Three failures compounded: 5g's hash did not see the file, audit-system check 1 only asked whether it EXISTS, and test-gates.py passed because it invokes gate-b.py by absolute path — proving the script works while proving nothing about whether anything calls it. The same held for .github/workflows/ci.yml, where deleting a step removes an enforcement layer without touching a single .py. The two files where one deleted line disables the most enforcement were the two the hash did not watch. os.listdir was also flat, leaving validation/adapters/carbon-react.py — the script with the worst defect record here — unhashed.
corrections.class: a guard that watched the checks and not the thing that makes them run
corrections.found_by: system-keeper, dispatched to attack check 5g itself on the grounds that installing a rule demanding independent attack, while exempting that rule from it, is self-refuting. Its verdict was 'A PROCESS PROMPT' — not theatre, not enforcement. Its first probe also did not fire at all: three reports written earlier the same day, listed in attestation.json as attesting the PREVIOUS hash, were reused to clear a later change, because attested_by was never dereferenced.
corrections.verifies: New check 2b requires the hooks to be REGISTERED, not merely present: gate-b.py under PreToolUse and session-check.py under Stop, with an empty permissions block reported separately. Negative-tested 2026-09-01 — deleting the hooks block now produces 2 BLOCKERS where it previously produced silence. 5g now walks validation/ and .claude/hooks/ recursively and includes settings.json, ci.yml and the contracts the checks read, so the wiring is inside the hash. An attesting report must CONTAIN THE CURRENT HASH, which closes three defeats found in one audit — a zero-byte file passed, an 'audit-TODO-placeholder' passed, and same-day reports were reused for later changes — and removes the wall-clock dependence that made the same commit green one day and red the next.
corrections.note: The honest limit is recorded in attestation.json rather than softened: this is a PROCESS PROMPT. Editing the recorded hash silences it and nothing detects that. It raises the cost of skipping the step and cannot make skipping impossible. The auditor's closing line is the one to keep: 'this report satisfies check 5g purely on the strength of its filename, and would have done so had I written nothing in it' — true when written, and the reason the hash-in-report requirement now exists.

corrections.defect: validation/metrics/ has been recording gate counts of 0/0/0/0 for five days. collect-metrics.py parses the NEWEST validation/reports/*__system-audit.md, and the newest such report is dated 2026-08-27 — so every snapshot since has reported the gate state of 2026-08-27 while appearing to describe its own day. corrections.verifies: FIXED and CHECKED 2026-09-02. collect-metrics.py no longer parses a report file: from_audit() runs `audit-system.py --json` as a subprocess and reads counts from that run, and on failure records verdict UNAVAILABLE with null counts rather than zeros — zero is a measurement, null is an admission, and conflating them was half the defect. corrections.logged now comes from validation/corrections.json (28) instead of the gitignored memory/corrections.md (4), which would have read 0 in any fresh clone including CI. The hardcoded "promoted": 0 was deleted rather than kept as a literal dressed as a count. corrections.defect: Hands-on capture was being run on a single browser surface, and that surface was the worst available choice for visual claims. The client's own Chrome carries third-party extensions (a 'Directo' deals panel, a 'vio' price bar) that inject UI into competitor pages. A programmatic check for injected overlays returned ZERO — they sit in shadow DOM or extension iframes that page-context selectors cannot reach — so any screenshot-derived observation could silently attribute a third-party overlay to a competitor, and nothing in the method would have caught it.
corrections.class: a capture surface that cannot see its own contamination
corrections.found_by: The client, by asking whether the inspector MCP was being used at all. It was not. Checking it revealed a SECOND browser — signed out, extension-clean, with network inspection — which turned a single contaminated surface into a matched pair: control and treatment. The first controlled run immediately produced a result no single session could: loyalty membership changes Booking.com's ranking surface by exactly one axis, and that axis is another price axis.
corrections.verifies: UNCHECKED as a validator, but now a standing rule in two places that are actually read: ART-024 section 4.1b, and a CLAUDE.md section loaded every turn. The residual blindness is stated rather than solved — the inspector cannot see authenticated flows and the authenticated browser cannot see network traffic, so network evidence about a PERSONALISED response is unavailable.

corrections.defect: ART-024 section 5.2 mandates that every observation carry a confidence of exactly Verified / Likely / Not Verified. Across 50 capture files and 170 confidence values the round recorded Verified 169 times, Likely once, and Not Verified zero times. A field that takes one value 99.4% of the time carries no information, and the dashboard built on top of it would have rendered a confidence encoding that discriminates nothing.
corrections.class: a required field that could not vary, so it stopped being a signal
corrections.found_by: dashboard-analyst, while building the findings board. It went to render the tri-state, found the data does not contain it, and said so rather than rendering three tiers where the underlying data has one. The main session then re-derived the counts and confirmed.
corrections.root_cause: The tri-state was designed for DESK research, where Likely and Not Verified are the normal outputs — a vendor claim, an inference from marketing copy, an absence in a web search. A HANDS-ON round produces first-hand observation or nothing, and first-hand observation is Verified by the plan's own definition. The scale did not fail; it was the wrong scale for the method.
corrections.what_actually_varied: Scope, not confidence. One render, one route, one locale, one moment, one competitor — that is what differs between a strong finding and a thin one here, and the round DID capture it, in scope_limit and caveat fields, on most findings. The useful signal was recorded in the right place and the mandated field was left carrying nothing.
corrections.verifies: UNCHECKED. The fix is not to enforce the tri-state — that would produce theatre. It is to REPLACE it for hands-on rounds with a scale that varies: something like corroboration count (how many independent captures support this) and reach (one render / one route / one locale / cross-competitor). ART-024 section 5.2 should be amended before round 2, not enforced.

corrections.defect: WORLD.json — the RAG corpus generated for retrieval — holds 117 chunks where CAPTURE-INDEX.json holds 121 findings. The 4 missing rows are, without exception, the round's own self-corrections: correction_to_own_earlier_claim (Expedia One Key was mis-framed), CORRECTION_to_F28 (Google Track-prices is gated per vertical, not per account), method_correction (Kayak's empty text sweep was not absence), and F71_AIRCOVER_IS_NOT_SHOWN_AT_THE_DECISION_REFUTES_PRIOR_CLAIM (a prior-round headline claim that did not survive contact with the product). WORLD.json declares itself 'GENERATED from the capture files' and 'regenerable from them', and nothing in its $comment, purpose, authority or coverage_warning says it is a subset. An agent retrieving from the corpus cannot see anywhere the round corrected itself. Separately, the index id CORRECTION_to_F28 does not match its capture key CORRECTION_to_finding_F28, so a naive resolver reports the content missing when it is present. EXTENDED 2026-09-07, after Phase 2 triage: the gap is two gaps, not one, and it is worse than 'four self-corrections were dropped'. WORLD's 117 reconciles as 112 unique numbered findings + F-108 counted TWICE + 4 unnumbered records. So one NUMBERED finding is absent from the retrieval corpus — F-71, the AirCover refutation — and it is load-bearing: recommendation 4 and pain point 4 both rest on it. An agent retrieving from WORLD.json cannot reach the evidence under two of the board's own conclusions, and separately sees F-108 twice.
corrections.class: a generated corpus that is a silent subset of its own index — and the omitted rows are exactly the corrections
corrections.found_by: the main session, during ART-026 v2 Phase 0, by set arithmetic on the two files rather than by reading either. Not found by reading WORLD.json, which looks complete. The second gap — F-71 missing and F-108 duplicated — was found by research-synthesizer during Phase 2 triage, independently of the first, and confirmed by the main session.
corrections.root_cause: All 4 omitted rows carry claim: 'see capture file' — a pointer where the claim text should be. The generator evidently skipped rows whose claim was not text, which is defensible in isolation. What is not defensible is skipping silently: the corpus states no row count, no subset warning, and no list of what it dropped. The selection rule and the disclosure rule were treated as the same decision, and only the first was made.
corrections.what_actually_varied: Nothing about the findings. The content of all 4 exists in full in the capture files and was verified present there during Phase 0. Only the corpus is short.
corrections.verifies: PARTIAL. The reconciliation is checked and reproducible, and confirms the gap is exactly 4 and that v1's build-dashboard.py restored exactly those 4 as hand-written stubs (cross-checked: the stubs invented nothing — every claim and evidence string in them was located verbatim in the capture files). NOT yet fixed at source: WORLD.json is still short by 4 and still carries no subset warning. Regenerating it is round-2 work on the generator, not a hand edit — hand-editing a file whose header says it is never hand-written would make the record worse. The F-71 absence and the F-108 duplication were confirmed by the main session against both files on 2026-09-07 and are unfixed: regenerating WORLD.json is generator work owed to round 2, and hand-editing a file whose header says it is never hand-written would make the record worse.
corrections.check_note: Asserts the CAPTURE-INDEX and WORLD row sets and reports the difference; resolves every pointer row against its capture file and fails loudly when content is not found.

corrections.defect: The confidence field is not the tri-state ART-024 section 5.2 mandates, and not the near-constant C-042 described either. Across the 121 CAPTURE-INDEX rows there are 14 distinct confidence strings: 101 are exactly 'Verified'; 13 are one-off sentences that state what specifically was and was not verified (e.g. 'Verified for the mechanism and the unit price. UNKNOWN for the caps.'); and 7 are the literal string 'see capture file' — a pointer occupying the slot where a rating belongs. For 7 of the 8 rows needing resolution the pointed-to block states no confidence of its own, so the only value available is the capture file's FILE-LEVEL confidence, which rates the capture and not the finding. v1's build-dashboard.py assigned 'Verified' to those rows without recording that the value was file-level.
corrections.class: a mandated categorical field carrying free prose in 13 cases and a pointer in 7 — so it cannot be encoded without guessing
corrections.found_by: the main session, while planning ART-026 v2's confidence chart. The chart could not be specified without deciding what the buckets were, and the buckets did not exist. Counting the strings, rather than assuming the schema held, is what surfaced it.
corrections.root_cause: Two different failures wearing one field. The 13 prose values are the round doing the right thing in the wrong slot — the real signal is scope, exactly as C-042 concluded, and it was written into confidence because there was nowhere else to put it. The 7 pointers are a stub that was never filled: the writer deferred to the capture file and nothing ever came back to resolve it. Both survived because nothing validates the field against an enumeration.
corrections.what_actually_varied: Note for anyone comparing with C-042: that record counted 170 confidence values across the capture FILES and found 169 Verified / 1 Likely. This record counts 121 rows in the INDEX. Different denominators, no contradiction — the single Likely does not appear in the index at all.
corrections.verifies: CHECKED for classification and resolution: 101 + 13 + 7 = 121, zero unclassifiable, 8 of 8 pointer rows resolved to real content in their capture files. NOT fixed at source: CAPTURE-INDEX.json still holds the 7 pointers. The fix is not to overwrite them with 'Verified' — that is precisely the promotion this record exists to catch. ART-024 section 5.2 must be amended before round 2 to replace the tri-state with a scale that varies, per C-042's own conclusion, and the 13 prose values are the specification for what that scale needs to express.
corrections.check_note: Classifies every confidence string by SHAPE alone — equals 'Verified' / starts with 'Verified' and carries more / is a pointer / anything else — and exits non-zero on any string it cannot place, so nothing is guessed into a bucket. Output: confidence-reconciliation.json, carrying confidence_class on all 121 rows, the full qualifying sentence on each of the 13, and an explicit confidence_provenance on each resolved pointer.

corrections.defect: Two of ART-026 v2's six charts — ch-themes and ch-matrix — bucket 121 `theme` strings into 11 categories, and the theme field had never been audited. Phase 0 had established, for the confidence field, that bucketing a free-text field without a mechanical audit is inference on evidence; the same discipline was never applied to theme. The consequence is visible on the board: all three disruption findings (F-56 Iberia, F-107 Qatar, F-113 American) are filed under `loyalty-and-retention`, so the matrix rendered `Iberia x Disruption & protection` and `Qatar x Disruption & protection` as EMPTY while the same board devotes an entire figure to those two disruption sweeps. A reader would conclude the round never examined Iberia's or Qatar's disruption handling, which inverts the actual coverage. An audit comparing each finding's theme against its own author-written id found that among the 29 rows the check can speak about, 14 — 48.3% — are filed under a theme their own identifier contradicts.
corrections.class: a second free-text field bucketed into categories without the audit the first one got
corrections.found_by: design-critic, on the first adversarial pass ever run against ART-026 — a pass ADR-021 item 4 has required since the ADR was accepted and which had never been performed. It reached the finding by reading the board's own embedded CSV rather than by reading the charts. The main session then confirmed it against WORLD.json and wrote the audit.
corrections.root_cause: Phase 0's lesson was recorded as being about the confidence field rather than about free-text fields generally. Having audited one field and found it unreliable, the correct inference was that neighbouring hand-assigned fields are also unreliable until checked. Instead the lesson stayed attached to the field where it was learned, and the next chart built on the next unaudited field.
corrections.what_actually_varied: Nothing about the underlying findings. Every disruption finding exists, is captured, and is cited correctly elsewhere on the board. Only the label is wrong, and only the two charts that read the label were affected.
corrections.verifies: CHECKED as a measurement, FIXED by demotion rather than by re-labelling. Re-theming 121 findings by hand would be exactly the inference this record exists to prevent, so the theme field is unchanged. What changed is what the two charts are permitted to claim: ch-matrix's caption no longer says an empty cell means nothing was captured — it says nothing carried that theme label — and names the Iberia/Qatar disruption case as the worked example. ch-themes now states that its bars count labels, not subjects. NOT fixed at source: the theme field remains unreliable and a round-2 re-theming against a written taxonomy is owed.
corrections.check_note: Compares two fields the record already contains — a finding's theme and its own id — and never reads claim prose or re-themes anything. Output: theme-audit.json. Reports a LOWER BOUND: 92 of 121 ids name no theme at all and are counted 'unknown', never 'agrees'.

corrections.defect: F-61 (captures/05-skyscanner/01-site-tree-and-undecided-traveller.json) claims 'Three competitors, one browser session, one afternoon — and each asserts a different location for the same traveller', and its evidence array attributes the string 'Estás en Toronto Todos los aeropuertos' to a GOOGLE TRAVEL AI planner. The capture that actually records that string is captures/04-kayak/03-ai-planner-and-first-empty-state.json, whose competitor field is Kayak and whose url is kayak.es/ai — it is KAYAK's AI planner (F-41). No Google Travel capture in the round records any location assertion at all; searched all Google captures for 'Estás en', 'You are in', 'Toronto' and 'ubicación': zero matches. So the finding names three competitors where the evidence supports two, and one of the two disagrees with ITSELF (Kayak's planner says Toronto while Kayak's flight search pre-fills Madrid). The board renders this as pain point 8, which inherits the misattribution verbatim.
corrections.class: a verbatim observation attributed to the wrong named company, and propagated to the board
corrections.found_by: research-synthesizer, during the Phase 1 corroboration sweep. It was not looking for this — it was searching for evidence that would corroborate pain-8, opened the primary capture behind the quoted string, and found the string belonged to a different product. The main session then confirmed it by searching every Google capture for a location assertion and finding none.
corrections.root_cause: F-61 is a CROSS-COMPETITOR synthesis written inside one competitor's capture file, citing two other competitors' captures from memory rather than by resolving them. The round's own rule that a claim must resolve to a capture was followed for the file path and not for the attribution inside it. Nothing checks that the competitor named in an evidence line matches the competitor field of the capture that line points at.
corrections.what_actually_varied: The observation is real and correctly recorded where it was first captured (F-41, Verified, Kayak). Only the re-statement in F-61 moves it to the wrong company. The underlying pain — products asserting a traveller's location and getting it wrong — survives; its shape changes from 'three products disagree' to 'one product contradicts itself and a second disagrees with both', which the finder noted is arguably sharper.
corrections.check_note: NOT a check for this defect — no check exists yet. The prepared input is listed so the class is traceable. What is owed: a validator that, for every evidence line naming a competitor, resolves the capture it cites and fails when the capture's competitor field disagrees. That check would have caught this and nothing in the repository performs it today.
corrections.verifies: FOUND and CONFIRMED, NOT YET FIXED. The capture files are immutable source and are not edited. The board's pain-8 rendering must be corrected and F-61 re-stated before ART-026 v2 goes to Gate A. Attribution errors about named companies are the most damaging class of defect this project can produce, because they are quotable and wrong.

corrections.defect: The evidence-chain chart in ART-026 v2, and the audit that preceded it, counted only references of the form F-nnn when measuring what each conclusion rests on. Every conclusion ALSO cites capture-file paths in the same sources list, and those are equally valid evidence references. The effect: every conclusion's evidence base was under-counted (insight-4 shows 3 F-refs against 4 capture paths; rec-3 and rec-6 each cite one finding id and two capture files), and pain-9 — which cites a capture path and no finding id at all — resolved to zero references and was silently DROPPED from the chart. The chart renders 25 conclusions where the board has 26.
corrections.class: a graph built from one of the two reference formats its own data uses
corrections.found_by: research-synthesizer during Phase 1, which reported that 'single_capture: 9' was mislabelled because rec-3 and rec-6 each list two capture files, and that pain-9 cites zero findings and is absent from the fragile list. The main session confirmed by counting both formats across all 26 conclusions.
corrections.root_cause: The graph builder used one regex for finding ids and treated its output as the complete citation set, because the first several conclusions inspected happened to cite finding ids. The sources field was never enumerated to see what shapes it actually contains — the same failure as C-044 and C-045, on a third field, and this time committed by me rather than inherited.
corrections.what_actually_varied: Nothing about the evidence. Every citation is present and correct in the data; only the counting was partial. The headline consequence is that 'nine conclusions rest on a single capture' overstates the fragility, and one conclusion is invisible in a chart whose whole purpose is to show what rests on what.
corrections.check_note: Extended so the chain figure must contain a node for every conclusion the board renders, and fails when the two counts disagree. The count itself now reads both reference formats.
corrections.verifies: FIXED and CHECKED. The chain counts finding ids and capture paths, pain-9 appears, and the verifier fails if the chart's conclusion count ever diverges from the board's again.
